newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Earthquake shakes Seoul; no injuries reported.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake shakes Seoul; no injuries reported.

text.p: A rare earthquake measuring about 4.4 on the Richter scale shook the South Korean capital of Seoul on Friday, but there were no immediate reports of injuries or damage, a Meteorological Agency spokesman said.
The spokesman said the epicentre of the earthquake was near the town of Yongwol in eastern Kangwan province, about 160 kilomtres (100 miles) from Seoul.
He said the temblor, which lasted for about 17 seconds, happened at 1.10 p.m. (0410 GMT).
Seoul residents said the capital was rarely shaken by earthquakes and the telephone switchboard of the Meteorological Agency that monitors seismic activity was jammed with calls.
The jolt was severe enough to rattle computers on desks in central Seoul office buildings.
